nodes.name: Watts-type sulfate bath electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Ni-Co alloy is electrodeposited from modified Watts (sulfate-chloride) bath where nickel sulfate and cobalt sulfate are primary sources of Ni and Co ions respectively, chloride ions provide good solution conductivity and aid nickel anode dissolution, boric acid serves as buffering agent. Soluble Ni and Co anodes used in acidic electrolyte.

unit_operations.name: Anode dissolution
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: soluble Ni and Co anodes are used in an acidic electrolyte

unit_operations.name: Cathodeposition
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: Ni and Co deposition at cathode workpiece

nodes.source_text: The sulfate based Watts bath, introduced in 1916, remains the most popular electrolyte... Nickel sulfate and cobalt sulfate are the primary sources of Ni and Co ions, respectively, chloride ions provide good solution conductivity

nodes.name: Chloride bath electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Ni-Co coatings obtained from chloride baths consisting of nickel chloride and cobalt chloride. Sodium chloride and ammonium chloride utilized as supporting agents to enhance cathodic current efficiency. Trisodium citrate sometimes employed as complexing agent for Ni and Co ions.

unit_operations.name: Electrolyte preparation
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: Sodium chloride and ammonium chloride are often utilised as supporting agents

unit_operations.name: Complexing
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: trisodium citrate is sometimes employed as a complexing agent

nodes.source_text: The NieCo coatings obtained from chloride baths have been studied... This bath consists of nickel chloride and cobalt chloride. Sodium chloride and ammonium chloride are often utilised

nodes.name: Sulfamate bath electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Ni-Co alloy electrodeposited from sulfamate bath where nickel sulfamate Ni(NH2SO3)2·4H2O (300-450 g dm^-3) and cobalt sulfamate Co(NH2SO3)2 (2.5-450 g dm^-3) act as sources of Ni and Co ions. NiCl2·6H2O (0-30 g dm^-3), CoCl2·6H2O (0-15 g dm^-3), H3BO3 (30 g dm^-3) added. High solubility enables high current densities.
nodes.source_text: Table 2 Sulfamate bath: Ni(NH2SO3)2·4H2O 300-450 g dm^-3, Co(NH2SO3)2 2.5-450 g dm^-3, H3BO3 30 g dm^-3, T 40-60°C, pH 3.0-5.4, j 2-15 A dm^-2

nodes.name: Acetate bath electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Ni-Co alloy electrodeposited from acetate-based bath using nickel acetate Ni(CH3CO2)2·4H2O and cobalt acetate Co(CH3CO2)2·4H2O as sources.
nodes.source_text: The sources of Ni and Co in the electrolyte were nickel acetate (Ni(CH3CO2)2·4H2O) and cobalt acetate (Co(CH3CO2)2·4H2O)

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni has face-centered cubic (fcc) crystal structure. Co has hexagonal close packed (hcp) structure below 417°C and fcc above 417°C. NiCo alloys form solid solutions throughout concentration range.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ni belongs to the transition group... face-centered cubic (fcc) crystal structure... Co can take two different crystalline structures; hexagonal closed packed (hcp; ε-Co) at T < 417 °C , and fcc; α-Co) at 417 °C : < T : < 1493 °C... Ni and Co form solid solutions (α-Co, α-Ni) throughout the range of concentration.
